title: Sketch-Based Replay Projection for Continual Learning

problem.claim: Replay-based continual learning methods can mitigate forgetting, but their performance may deteriorate when replayed data does not effectively represent all experienced data.

gap.claim: Existing replay methods need to better preserve the distribution of the original data stream within stored memory.

contributions.claim: The authors propose Sketch-based Replay Projection (SRP), a method for capturing and retaining the original data stream's distribution within stored memory.
SRP introduces a sketch-based sample selection technique that approximates feature distributions within distinct tasks and captures a wide distribution of examples for replay.

SRP introduces a data compression method that projects examples into a reduced-dimensional space while preserving inter-example relationships, emphasizing inter-class disparities, and maintaining memory requirements similar to existing replay methods.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that SRP enhances replay diversity and improves the performance of existing replay models.

narrative_sequence.summary: Continual learning trains models sequentially on task streams while retaining previously learned knowledge.
Replay methods mitigate forgetting, but insufficiently representative replay data can reduce performance.
SRP is proposed to preserve the original data stream's distribution in memory and extends existing replay frameworks through a two-fold approach.
The approach combines task-level sketch-based sample selection with compressed projections that preserve relationships and emphasize class disparities.
The authors report improved replay diversity and performance for existing replay models.

source_observation.claim: Replay performance may decline when stored examples do not represent the full experienced data distribution.

interpretation.claim: Memory-constrained replay should prioritize distributional coverage rather than only retaining arbitrary past examples.

application.claim: For continual-learning replay buffers, select examples that approximate task-level feature distributions and preserve diverse class representations.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that distribution-preserving selection improves every continual-learning setting or replay framework.
